page.overview:
What is Half-orcs?

Half-orcs, also called Orc-men, were a crossbred-race of Orcs and Men first conceived by the Dark Lords Morgoth and Sauron. They were later predominantly used by the corrupted Wizard Saruman, in the War of the Ring, as soldiers in his army, but also as spies in Eriador.

During the Elder Days, Half-orcs first appeared through some union of Orcs and of Men, the latter of which had been bent to an "Orc-level of mind and habits" by Morgoth and his agents, such as Sauron. Centuries afterwards in the Third Age, Sauron's vassal, Saruman, replicated these methods, which he had learned from his master or otherwise rediscovered through his own researches, and made his own Half-orcs beneath Isengard. Saruman originally commanded some Uruks which had come down from the Misty Mountains to serve the Wizard as merceneries. He also later bred his own Uruks, and this was kept secret from the White Council at the time. Aragorn noticed something different about the Uruks compared to standard Orcs, stating that "Their gear is not after the manner of Orcs at all!" He noticed that their bows were like those of men. According to Treebeard and later Gamling, this kind of Saruman's minions could endure daylight, unlike the common Orcs. The White Wizard used Half-orcs as warriors to attack Rohan on the Dark Lord's behalf, but also as his own spies throughout Eriador, especially in the Shire's vicinity, in hopes of capturing the Ring-bearer first. One of the latter kind was the Squint-eyed Southerner, an outcast from Dunland who looked "more than half like a goblin". He initially procured pipe-weed and acted as Saruman's most-trusted informant on the Shire's affairs, until he was discovered by the Nazgûl and coerced into becoming their spy in Bree.

During the War of the Ring, Half-orcs, together with Northern Orcs, Dunlendings and Uruk-hai, were part of Saruman's army that clashed with Théodred's forces in the First Battle of the Fords of Isen; it was one axe-wielding Orc-man that mortally-wounded the prince, accomplishing the special task given by the White Wizard. These creatures were later part of the 10,000 warriors sent against Théoden's people at Helm's Deep, Alongside the rest of Saruman's minions, the Half-orcs were crushed at the Battle of the Hornburg, being either slain before the fortress walls or in the Huorn forest.

Other Half-orcs perished with the remaining Orcs of Isengard in the pits, mostly because of the huge flood the Ents of Fangorn Forest made when they descended upon Isengard with wrath. But those who had been sent westwards were spared the corrupted Wizard's defeat. Banding together with Ruffians, they became enforcers for Lotho Sackville-Baggins, Saruman's secret ally in the Shire, and imposed his policies; following Lotho's death, they fell back under the authority of the exiled Saruman, whom they called "Sharkey", and helped him exact his petty vengeance against Gandalf by terrorizing the local Hobbits. The Half-orcs were slain, however, along with most of the vile Men in the Battle of Bywater by the oppressed halflings and buried in the Battle Pit.
